idiom_name: virtual base class + factory keyed on the type column
implementation_notes: C++ provides the object side for free - virtual functions give dynamic dispatch through a base pointer/reference - but nothing in the standard library or dominant libraries maps a hierarchy to a table, so STI is a hand-written mapper: one row struct with the union of columns, a type column, and a factory that reads the tag and constructs the matching derived class behind a base-class pointer. Choose this form when subtypes carry behaviour and the hierarchy is open-ended; pick the variant realization below when the set of cases is closed and you would rather have exhaustive, value-based dispatch.
pitfalls: Dynamic subtype objects need a virtual destructor and clear ownership; a mapper that returns raw base pointers is the usual leak/UB source, so return smart pointers.
Object slicing: copying a Manager into an Employee value silently discards the subtype; map into pointers or references, never by value.
The factory's if/else chain is the single point where the discriminator is interpreted - an unhandled value must throw, because the database will not guarantee it maps to a class.

variants.name: Closed hierarchy as std::variant visited with std::visit
variants.implementation_notes: For a closed hierarchy, std::variant is the type-safe union that replaces the virtual hierarchy: the variants are the subtypes, the discriminator is the active alternative, and std::visit dispatches exhaustively over them. The mapper still owns the table side (one wide row, one type column), but it fills the variant instead of allocating polymorphic objects, which removes the ownership and slicing traps at the cost of fixing the set of subtypes at compile time.
pitfalls: std::visit requires every alternative to be handled (or a generic lambda); adding a subtype to the table without adding it to the variant is a compile error - good, but it means the table and the variant must be changed together.
A default-constructed variant holds the first alternative: mapping a row must assign the correct alternative explicitly, otherwise the discriminator is silently ignored.
std::variant cannot represent 'no value'; if the discriminator can be absent, the first alternative must be std::monostate.
